I've been more punky listener of music since my high school days, but after I started a Ska band in 2008 I was quickly introduced into Psychobilly/Horrorbilly. (IE. Creepshow, Nekromantics, Reverend Horton Heat, etc...) and as I listened to these band Pandora or Itunes suggestions kept bringing me to older music that kind of inspired these other bands, Dion and the Belmonts, The Four Tops, and the like. I'd always dismissed these artists as Old and never given them my full attention. It also didn't help that Oldies radio doesn't play a lot of their music, or didn't in my area. But after giving these bands a listen now, I'm amazed I never gave them any love earlier. Have you ever had a newly discovered genre or band lead you into a whole new world of music?
Psychobilly got me into the Oldies, has a genre/band ever led you to discovering new music?

I typically stay within that band's genre when I look up similar sounds. Like I've gone from edm stuff to Kraftwerk and Animal Collective to Mercury Rev. Other than that I'm pretty boring when it comes to discovering new music. I just look through new releases and look up interesting album art or jnteresting band names. I discovered Plebian Grandstand because their name made me chuckle, pretty good black metal band out of France.

I'm the same way. If the album art is awesome I'll give the band a chance.

Also if you want clever names, I suggest Slugdge - Gastronomicon The entire album is about a slug.

I stumbled upon a song by Ramona Falls that particularly struck me. It's been several years since then, and my taste shifted from primarily electric/Digital to anything that sounds good because of it, and by that I mean I don't really dislike any pieces unless I think they're poorly structured/timed.

But Ramona Falls led to finding Mother Mother, which I think has become my all time favorite band.
Stevie Nicks got me into Florence + The Machine. Queens of the Stone Age got me into Them Crooked Vultures.

I've always been into old school rock and roll and hip hop, and never really gave purely electronic music a chance. That is until I was turned on to C2C's album Tetra. The turntabling trio produced easily one of the most kinetic and vibey records I know of, and opened my eyes to the wonders of multi layered sampling. Now I have a great deal more respect for the beat makers and live jammers of the world, and couldn't be caught dead without SoundCloud.

I've discovered lots of new music through Red Hot Chili Peppers. Mainly their former guitarist's, John Frusciante, solo stuff that I would highly recommend. They also led me into p-funk, they have some really good music.
